svg.title: Separate Record Costs From Legal Cure Costs
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-separate-document-and-cure-costs; chapter number: 4; title: Separate Record Costs From Legal Cure Costs; subtitle: Different services carry different quoted costs and exclusions.; caption: GenealogyMagazine quotes ordinary copies; Jamel Gibbs quotes preliminary title searches; Alex Goldovansky on Logan Fullmer quotes mortgage-release work; Al Nicoletti on Courtney Fricke quotes a single probate.; assumptions note: GenealogyMagazine, Jamel Gibbs, Alex Goldovansky, and Al Nicoletti supply independent US-dollar price references. These are not components of a reported combined transaction budget and must not be summed into an asserted total.; note: Nicoletti explains that additional deceased owners and downstream estates multiply probate expense. Goldovansky notes lender-dependent difficulty and cases that cannot be resolved.; chart type: stacked_comparison; total range: No combined total reported; independent quoted prices in USD; buckets: label: Ordinary courthouse copy per page; low: 1.0; high: 1.0; notes: GenealogyMagazine reports usually $1.00 per page, except vital records; certification costs more.; label: Preliminary professional title search; low: 100; high: 150; notes: Jamel Gibbs gives this approximate provider-dependent range for preliminary screening, not the full purchase search and process.; label: Mortgage-release work; low: 150; high: 175; notes: Alex Goldovansky quotes this all-in range depending on the lender; private creditors and deceased lenders can be more difficult.; label: Single probate proceeding; low: 4000; high: 4500; notes: Al Nicoletti gives this approximate single-probate example. Complete title and property investigation before authorizing paid probate work.
